items: The Listen window now shows exactly what is prepared for your phone: for every queued book, which part of the book the audio covers, how many passages and how much listening time are coming up, prepared on the computer and already in the cloud, with totals, the space used, the voice, and the books that come later or were left out. You can prepare several queues at once (each gets its own hours ahead, nearest passages first), and set the hours and the cloud limit right there. On the phone, a table shows per book what is in the cloud and what is already downloaded, and you can pick which queue to listen to.

Phone listening is clearer and quicker. Your computer now uploads audio a few passages at a time, so the phone gets the first ones within minutes instead of after the whole window is rendered. The Listen window shows, for each queued book, how many passages are ahead, rendered and in the cloud, and says why a book was left out (for example, its text isn't on the computer). On the phone it shows which computer prepared the audio and when, and warns if the browser can't play it.
Settings has a "Find a setting" box that filters the rows of each section, and on a phone, pop-up windows now fill the screen.

New menus, organised by what you're doing: File, Reader, Library, Listen, Practice, Settings, Extras and Help. The panel switches (Fast Reader, Lines, ToC, Stats, Index, Avatars, Chips, Incognito) now live in one Panels menu, so the bar fits on one row.
One Settings window: General, This tab, New-tab defaults, Fonts, Audio, Typing, Comfort & breaks, Sync & data and Book groups are sections across its top, in a single tab.
On the phone, a tab bar along the bottom: Reader, Library, Listen, Practice and More.
Trackyread's views are grouped into Books, Queues, Insights, AI and Import / Export, so they no longer scroll sideways on a phone.
Right-click a tab (long-press on a phone) for two new options: close the others that are in a queue, or close the others that aren't.

Preparing audio for your phone is now one checklist: on your computer open Audio → Listen to the Queue & Prepare Phone Audio, and tick off sign-in, sync machine, voice, queue and rendering in one place.

The start screen has buttons to open a book, paste text, open your library or listen. Rarely used tools (teleprompter, avatars, crosshairs, reading cursor, biometric controls, HTML tools) moved to a new Extras menu.
Trackyread's AI page now only sends work to your AI runner: the copy-and-paste, direct-API, manual snapshot and inbox options are gone, and syncing is automatic so it is no longer listed there.

Listen to your queue on the phone without the book files: Audio → Listen to the Queue plays the passages your computer rendered ahead, with lock-screen controls and speed. Your place moves as you listen, and finishing a book marks it read in Trackyread, on every device. Your phone and computer now also sync whenever you come back to the app, so Trackyread, its AI analysis and your queues are up to date on both.

Your read-aloud and narration sessions now go to your own cloud folder too (when you are signed in), so SpeechImprover can analyse them on any device, no folder to pick. Sessions you already recorded on this device are sent once.

Cowork now runs through your cloud: requests, replies and the activity snapshot go to your private app folder, where your AI runner answers them, so the Cowork page works the same on a phone as on the computer. Sign in once on the Cowork page instead of choosing a folder. A reply applied (or discarded) on one device is never applied again on another.

Cloud sync is safer: every sync reads the cloud copy first and merges it item by item, so a phone that was offline can no longer overwrite newer reading, notes or library changes from another device, and a deletion stays deleted. Sync now uses the cloud you chose once for every app (Google Drive); the old option of syncing through a folder on this computer is gone, and Back up and Restore are one Sync now button.

Numbers now follow your language (a decimal comma in French, for example). Dates and times show as 2026-11-21 and 14:05 everywhere, or in your region’s style if you choose Regional under the font picker. Arabic, Persian and Urdu lay the whole app out right to left; a book or typing passage keeps its own direction.

The rest of Tachyread now speaks your language: Help, Grab Text (OCR), the biometric and camera controls, eye warm-up, comfort reminders and the avatar and font pickers. The narrated Help slideshow still speaks English, since its voices are English-only.

Audio is now in your language too: the Audiobook Command Centre, narration and recording, audio settings, audiobook export and sync, and the reading-aloud voice feedback. Voice names stay as they are, since narration tags use them.
Typing is now in your language too: the typing screen and its results, Typing Progress, plans and settings, Flow Writer, the span drill, vocabulary, dictation and pronunciation.
Trackyread now speaks your language too: the library, queues, timeline, analytics, notes, the tech tree and the AI / Cowork page.

Every theme picker now starts with the shared themes every app offers: Light, Dark, Midnight, Slate, Ocean, Forest, Ember, Gold, Synthwave, Terminal, Paper, Pastel, Mono and High contrast. Light, Dark, Midnight, Slate and Forest now use the shared colours; all of Tachyread’s other themes are still there.

More of Tachyread now speaks your language: the reading screen, the status bar, the contents, index and companion panes, and the Find, History, Statistics, Notes, Proper Names, HTML tools, OPDS, web-grab and other reader windows. A book keeps its own reading direction whatever language the menus are in.

Tachyread is starting to speak your language: menus, tabs, the controls and the Settings, Application settings, Data and Font manager windows now come in French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Croatian, German, Chinese, Ukrainian, Esperanto, Swahili, Hindi, Bengali, Indonesian, Urdu, Persian and Arabic (pick it under Settings → Application → App font). They are machine translated from English and unchecked; the rest of the app follows.

New Cowork operation: an AI review of your typing runs and reading-aloud sessions. Each gets a grade, what went well, what to fix and a next step, shown beside Tachyread's own score (Typing Progress has a new AI column). Schedule it and it runs after each session; undo removes it.
Scheduled Cowork replies now wait for your review before anything changes. Switch that off per report under AI / Cowork if you'd rather they apply themselves.
Tachyread now starts in light or dark to match your device, until you pick a theme yourself.
Menus and dialogs use Atkinson Hyperlegible by default. Change it under Settings → Application → App font; your own reading fonts still win.
Streaks, finish dates and daily totals follow your own calendar: reading late in the evening counts for that day.
A bar tells you when a new version is ready, and another shows up if something goes wrong, with a Reload button.
About Tachyread (in Application settings) shows the version, where your data lives, storage used and diagnostics.
The camera and OCR engines now load from Tachyread's own site.
Delete everything says clearly that other apps and your Drive copy are left alone.
Queues can fill themselves from a description, suggest moving a book to a better queue (without asking twice), and prepare spoiler-free notes before you start.
Files you moved out of your search folders no longer show their old location.
Add a whole folder of books to Trackyread without opening them.
Listen mode plays straight through a reading queue, with chapter and book skips on the lock screen.
Narration clips are stored 15 to 30 times smaller.
Reading aloud gives a presenting score from your camera.
